title: Derived balances, getTotalShares()
detects: The share-based spelling of derived balances, as Lido's stETH writes it. The contract stores a share count per holder and reports balanceOf as that share multiplied by the pooled total over the share total, so the getter answering proves the figure a wallet shows is computed rather than stored.
knownFalseNegative: The same caveat as meta-scaled-balance: this reads the accounting shape, not who moves the factor. On stETH the pooled total tracks validator rewards reported by an oracle quorum, which is not one address rewriting a balance at will. A rebasing token spelling the getter a third way reads absent, as every dictionary entry does until its spelling is added.

coversExamples.observed: getTotalShares() and getTotalPooledEther() both answer through the Aragon proxy; scaledTotalSupply() reverts

rationale: stETH is the largest token on Ethereum whose displayed balance moves without a transfer, and meta-scaled-balance does not read it: it answers getTotalShares(), not scaledTotalSupply(). Its implementation also sits behind an Aragon proxy that neither the EIP-1967 nor the zeppelinos slot points at, so the gap scan cannot see its selectors either. Without this file the clearest case of a derived balance on Ethereum reads as having nothing on the transparency axis.
